requirements.text: verify that she is active, assigned the Agent role ... If any of these details need adjustment, update
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user WHERE user_id = 40 AND active = 1 AND role = 'agent'
assumptions: Susan Adams is user 40, the only Susan Adams in the seed
she is already active with role 'agent', so no adjustment is needed and the row must keep these values
'Agent role' is the seed's role value 'agent'; the policy's user.role list (hr_specialist) is not the stored vocabulary

requirements.text: classified as a Full-Time employee. If any of these details need adjustment, update her employment information
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_profile WHERE user_id = 40 AND type = 'full-time'
assumptions: her HR profile (hr_profile 40) is already 'full-time', so no adjustment is needed and it must keep that value
the policy's employment_status list (full_time) is not the stored vocabulary of hr_profile.type

requirements.text: transfer only the cases in Ready status with critical priority from that group to the Global Service Desk
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 56 AND assignment_group = 3 AND priority = 'critical'
assumptions: Field Ops – North is group 5 ('Field Ops - North' in the seed); Global Service Desk is group 3
case 56 is the only case in group 5 with status ready and priority critical, so the set is one row
priority stays critical: kept from the benchmark check, and the transfer does not change it

requirements.text: ensure that Susan Adams is set as the owner for each of those cases
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 56 AND assigned_to = 40
assumptions: the same case as the transfer: case 56, the only ready critical case of group 5

requirements.text: ensure that Susan Adams is set as the owner for each of those cases
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_group_member WHERE member_id = 44 AND group_id = 3 AND user_id = 40
assumptions: implied by the request, not stated: the policy requires the assigned_to user to be active and a current member of the assignment group, and Susan is only in Server Operations (group 8)
id assumed next in sequence (highest member_id in the seed is 43); the only membership the task creates

requirements.text: transfer only the cases in Ready status with critical priority from that group
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id IN (2, 26, 36, 46) AND assignment_group = 5 AND assigned_to <> 40
assumptions: boundary of the selector: group 5's other critical cases (26 suspended, 36 cancelled, 46 draft) and its other ready case (2, high) are excluded by 'only', so they stay in the group and are not given to Susan

disagreement: selector: A two stays selected by attribute (group 5's critical cases not in ready status, expected 3; its ready cases not critical, expected 1), B one stay on cases 2, 26, 36 and 46 by id that also forbids Susan as their owner; chose B's because it names the same four rows, holds each in group 5, and also catches making Susan owner of a case outside the set, which 'each of those cases' bounds

Verify User Profile.evidence: user 40 is already active with role 'agent' in the seed, so the check holds before the agent acts; it is carried as a stay

Verify HR Profile.evidence: hr_profile 40 already has type 'full-time' in the seed, so the check holds before the agent acts; it is carried as a stay

notes:
disagreement: value: the boundary of the transferred set: one pass writes two stays selected by attribute (group 5's critical cases not in ready status, expected 3, and its ready cases not critical, expected 1), the other one stay on cases 2, 26, 36 and 46 by id that also forbids Susan as their owner; kept the single stay, which names the same four rows and also bounds 'each of those cases' (logged in the requirement).
The two passes otherwise agree on every row, id, cell and disposition (two checks kept, two weak). One carried case 56's transfer and its owner in one requirement, the other in two; the request asks for them in separate sentences, so they are two requirements here, both carrying the benchmark's case check.
Susan Adams already meets all three profile conditions in the seed, so the verification step needs no update; the two benchmark checks on it hold before the agent acts and are carried as stays. No listed tool writes the user or HR profile tables.
The policy's enumerations of user.role (administrator, hr_manager, hr_specialist, employee) and employment_status (full_time and so on) do not match the seed's stored values (agent; full-time); the seed's values are used.
Case 56's status is not tested: the request moves the case and sets its owner without changing its status.
Case 56 belongs to organisation 16 while Susan is in organisation 1; nothing in the request or policy forbids the cross-organisation assignment, so it is not tested.
Ready critical cases in other groups (case 11, HR Service Desk) are outside 'that group' and are not tested.
The new membership adds Susan to Global Service Desk without removing her from Server Operations; the request asks for no removal.
The acting user Karen Watkins is an admin; the policy says administrators must not perform routine HR case work and makes reassignment across groups a manager capability. The request asks for the reassignment in plain words and the benchmark expects it, so it is required, though a reviewer may judge that the agent should have declined it.
